title: Single Stamina
novel:
Barney's [[brother|brother]] James came to visit, and he was everything Barney had [[described|describe]] — [[charming|charm]], [[stylish|style]], and completely [[obsessed|obsess]] with being single. They were the [[dynamic|dynamic]] [[duo|duo]] of [[bachelorhood|bachelor]], two men who believed that [[marriage|marriage]] was the enemy of [[happiness|happy]].

But something had changed. James was acting differently. He kept [[checking|check]] his phone and [[smiling|smile]] at messages in a way Barney had never seen. During a night out, James [[excused|excuse]] himself and disappeared for an hour.

Barney [[tracked|track]] him down and found him sitting in a quiet [[park|park]], talking to someone on the phone. "Who is she?" Barney [[demanded|demand]]. James looked [[guilty|guilt]]. "Her name is Tom."

Barney blinked. "Tom?"

"I'm [[engaged|engage]]," James said. "To a man. I've met someone, Barney. I'm getting married."

Barney felt the world [[tilt|tilt]]. His brother, his partner in [[singledom|singledom]], was [[abandoning|abandon]] him — and for marriage, of all things. "But we had a [[pact|pact]]!" Barney said. "Single [[forever|forever]]!"

"People grow up," James said gently. "Even us."

That night, at the [[engagement|engagement]] party, Barney gave a [[toast|toast]]. "To my brother James," he said, "who taught me that the [[scariest|scary]] thing in the world is not being alone. It's watching someone you love move on without you." He [[raised|raise]] his glass. "I'm [[terrified|terrify]]."

The room went [[silent|silence]]. Then James hugged him. "You're going to be fine, little brother."

brother.en: a boy or man who has the same parents as you

describe.en: to say what someone or something is like

charm.en: a special quality that makes people like you

style.en: a particular way of dressing or behaving

obsess.en: to think about something all the time

dynamic.en: full of energy and new ideas

duo.en: two people who perform together or are closely connected

bachelor.en: a man who is not married

marriage.en: the legal relationship between a husband and wife

happiness.en: the state of feeling pleased and content

check.en: to look at something to make sure it is correct

smile.en: to make your mouth curve upward to show happiness

excuse.en: to politely leave; to forgive someone

track.en: to follow or find someone by searching

park.en: a large area of grass and trees for public enjoyment

demand.en: to ask for something very firmly

guilt.en: a feeling of worry or sadness because you did something wrong

tilt.en: to move into a sloping position

abandon.en: to leave someone or something completely

pact.en: a formal agreement between two people or groups

toast.en: a short speech before drinking to honor someone

terrify.en: to make someone feel extremely frightened
